03 / Inspect behavior, not just configuration

The code contains a trap with no timed recovery.

A shorter offer window feeds an existing history penalty. Lower rank can remove the very opportunities needed to earn acceptance credit.

01 / WINDOW

90 → 60 seconds

The same controlled 75-second answer changes from taken to missed.

02 / HISTORY

Miss = refusal

Both subtract 0.12. Taking a callout earns only 0.08.

03 / RANK

Someone else accepts

History still weighs 0.25. Dispatch stops offering after acceptance.

04 / RECOVERY

No offer, no credit

Quiet time alone does not improve a retained score. The aging TODO was never implemented.

Answer to engineering's question: an explicitly declined ping and a missed ping receive the same history treatment in this code. Whether that was intended is a product-policy question, not something the code can authorize.

What we proved

  • 16 controlled tests pass against unchanged routing source.
  • All 1,696 observed outcomes were replayed under three initial-score assumptions; the severe four end at modeled zero.
  • A responder can remain available/listed and still receive no offer when an earlier candidate accepts.

What we did not prove

  • Actual historical scores, answer times, candidate sets or deployed version.
  • That responders were automatically marked unavailable.
  • That restoring 90 seconds restores already lost priority.
  • That every lost offer was caused by this mechanism.

Reweighting reduced each miss's history contribution from 0.048 to 0.030; it did not increase the penalty mathematically. The timeout change and older recovery gap are distinct. Mechanism, source map and limits · Test evidence.

Five-minute walkthrough and decision boundaries
  1. Request access review from Kip's console.
  2. In Responder phone, acknowledge and confirm readiness.
  3. In Operations review, confirm all five fit and maintenance checks.
  4. Authorize the review, then demonstrate an eligible offer.
  5. Advance the demo 75 seconds and accept before the proposed 90-second deadline.

Also try expiry, changed fit, deliberate decline, a missed deadline and responder pause. Missing checks block authorization; changed fit withdraws the illustrative opportunity.

One appropriate offer within a two-hour review window and a 90-second offer are proposed evaluation values, not approved production policy. No routing code was changed or deployed.

How this reduces the chance of repeating the decision failure

01 / OWNER

Make accountability explicit

Name the team or role that owns the commitment and the next decision. A stakeholder mention alone does not establish ownership.

02 / OUTCOME

Define what success means

Require an observable outcome rather than a feature list. For Dispatch recovery, use the responder-access scorecard alongside acceptance; the checklist alone does not select the right metric.

03 / SCOPE

Expose a changing promise

Compare the opening commitment with requirements and delivery scope. Flag material drift before the team commits to the expanded work.

04 / PROBLEM

Put evidence before the build

Establish the customer problem before prescribing an app, a setting or another solution. Keep assumptions visible for the decision-maker.

Prevention requires follow-through. Review-checklist reviews product briefs; it does not monitor production routing, block releases or guarantee that this incident cannot recur. Ravi's responder-level measures, eligibility/delivery telemetry and engineering release/rollback validation are still needed.

Failure discipline: missing sources preserve the last complete baseline; source removal is not issue resolution; unchanged successful reviews stay quiet. Eighteen state-integrity tests passed. The helper validates evidence provenance and state, not the correctness of every semantic judgment.
